## Bottle 66

_by Kantiki Jayamana Whateva_

Out of the six people who even knew this was happening before I wrote this entry, the very first of those was me mum Merlynne Watson herself... as it was born in those days of talking philosophy and designing graphics on her turquoise gel-tab iMac. It got pushed to the side when I started hitchhiking in the summer of 2000, as I was living the adventure... _living the travels_.. . and those stories would be put in "[Landlore](landlore)" and not this book.

So _Bottle 66_ found itself gathering dust. But every once in a while, it'd come up again. Maybe just a quote or a thought on it. So I'd email it to myself, folder it, then forget it again.

In 2029 it will be 30-years old since conception.

In 2029 I'll be publishing the book itself. Rightfully so, it will certainly be among my set of traveling books, so it will have at least 100 physical editions printed with 80 of them traveling "out 'n about", then the other 20 given to friends, tribe, and family.

"Bottle 66" is just the codename for it, but it's actually stuck a long time right from the very start. Don't be too surprised if I keep it going right up to the finish line.

The book has at least five different ways to read the story, each with their own very different readings, starting out on the ocean near Venice Beach, California and diving deep into the deserts along Route 66. The Escheresque cover is no mistake, but instead encapsulates so much of the book without giving anything away.

Similar to "[Everything Will Be OK](everything-will-be-ok)", this one's been a long time coming and has an admixture of humor, but instead of sci-fi as with that other one, leans instead into spirituality and travel.

* * *

### Extended Exploration

I've already mentioned the non-fiction "[Landlore](landlore)" series of books, but it's always worth mentioning again since that series has been an ongoing source of inspiration that's bled into _Bottle 66_ over the years. Funnily enough, while perspective drawings are my favorite sketches, I rarely publish or share them. I mean, I friggin' love 'em! Planting two thumbtacks into a cutting board, taping down paper, then going to town with a ruler. I forget what PBS program it was, but I remember watching it as an early teenager and getting hooked immediately on this style of drawing. I'd already been inspired by M C Escher, himself, and that was enough to push me over the edge and get me hooked on the drug. Maybe one day I'll share more of those. Until that time, my [surreal fractalscapes](other-fractalscapes) might draw your eye along with my [pop art fractals](other-pop-art).
